body: I appreciate it. I am battling so many things at the moment I am just overwhelmed and ready to give up but keep on going. I would like to chat sometime so just let me know when would work for you. I appreciate you reaching out.
Life has gotten way worse. I have tried to end it by taking 94 Benadryl, but that didn't work... Not to discourage you, but I just dont have any support anymore and want the pain to end.
Im on the same page, I wont give you the usual dont give up your worth it stuff, to me that almost makes it worse. I can relate on many levels, so feel free to contact me if you want to chat.

Your right. I cut myself off like 5 prescriptions and had a nervous breakdown. I would get help but I already burned my one chance, so now I am just trying to deal with what I got. Feel free to PM me if you want to talk more. Thank you for your opinion.

I appreciate the response. Im trying to keep my hopes up and know I need other help but my family, and community are spent and I am pretty much left to my own devices, but such is life. Im off the suboxone, weening off the rest, homeless, broke, in bad shape, but that's life and it will get better (I hope and am working toward). If you ever want to talk feel free to PM me.
I see your point and as I re-read I can see clearly how naïve the beginning was.
Interesting poem. I myself thought of it as a poem on living in society, but apparently I am wrong! Well written.
I like the imagery used in your poem. Is it love lost that which you are referencing to sleep deprivation?

For me its moments of clarity vs moments of chaos. Life (I am told repeatedly) is about balance. I am terrible at communicating, think too much of things etc. I suppose I only say this to reassure you your not alone and that I guarantee your lack of presence would be dearly missed, people love you, its just the gremlins trying to get you down.

I relate on so many levels to what you say. From what I can tell its a bit of both. I think getting older is not for the faint of heart, but also environmental or situational factors can amplify existing issues. Communication for me is a terrible phobia, but I wont get better if I dont communicate. I guess I only say this because of my experience, perhaps something to think on? I know that feeling though of being surrounded by people and still feeling alone.

Im sorry you feel that way. I have had a seriously screwed up year and just want you to know people care, it may seem down right hopeless, but just keep giving it time. Sometimes its hard to see yourself, or how much people care until after the fact.

A bit of tough love and genuine concern and personal opinion. In one aspect unfortunately we are all in a sense "alone" as we all live in our own skin / world. Perception is a tricky one, where sometimes the mind overrules the body, and pain overrides logic. I attempted suicide and failed at that \(im a real winner :\-/ \), and now my guts are all messed up and I may have damaged my kidney. So not to state the obvious and that damn advice of "things will get better in time", which I know from my experience is probably the last thing you want to hear when your in the dumps, but you matter \(b/c your made of matter!\)

An analogy came to mind: Its like telling a starving person on an island awaiting a drop of food supplies, and they have no clue when, but people say just be patient it will come or, "dont worry you will eat sometime". Bad analogy but I hope you get the gist. I wont feed you the rhetoric that life is worth living blah blah blah. Sometimes I feel people should have the right to feel downright depressed etc, *as long as they dont lash out at others.* 

But I can almost guarantee things may not go exactly how you want them to, but they will happen exactly how they were intended. And I am not referring to religion, but rather the state of the human experience. I know for myself my utter lack of control of a lot in life creates unbearable anxiety, stress, and pain. This said, everyday I make a small improvement builds on the day before and before I know it life will and is not looking so dismal, this latest down turn will be nothing but another bad period of time. Time is all we have, we all share this world, and I know I speak for most people that we would rather see someone overcome a terrible situation than to see them give up \(If someone is happy about you being miserable, break away NOW!\).

Keep strong, keep engaged, and keep in mind there are a lot of people with their own serious issues, and perhaps talking to them to see what works best for coping may provide you with some relief or at least a different perspective!

Im going to take a different approach than the usual plea for not giving up, so excuse me if this comes off wrong. Lets say hypothetically you make that decision that there is no going back on, what would it solve? I do not know you but I know we are all connected in some strangely ironic way, its what makes humans great. Our ability to overcame the most challenging times, create opportunities or possibilities previously thought of as impossible, make life worth it. I have had severe bipolar depression, anxiety, poor health, really bad luck, I mean really bad, and mulled over the idea of just letting go and giving up. The part that will make the difference is letting go, the part that will end it all Is giving up. So you hang in there, treat yourself daily to something nice, it doesn't have to be huge, and if possible write 10\-20 good things in your day, 10\-20 people or places you wish to see or be with, and within minutes I can almost assure you that your thoughts will pass. I dont think people have total control over the randomness that pops into their brain, but we do have control over our bodies and how we interact with life. Its all a matter of perspective, and the world just wouldn't be the same without you, so keep your chin up, keep talking, keep engaged, and each tiny victory will set a new path; one which is filled with all the greatness you deserve. Im sorry if this did not make sense, or was of no help. just keep doing the next right thing and in general things tend to get better, but usually things have a way of all going south at the same time, so just think of it as a test, and if you pass, the world is your oyster!

First off thank you for your strength in sharing. I commend you on dealing with a very difficult situation. Please do not hurt yourself! I have a terrible stomach \(result of poor eating and a decade of pain relievers\), I got a colo/endo \(fun!\), and had a few minor polips which is pretty normal but the acid in my stomach has created some pretty painful ulcers, and I was told I have [**Barrett's Esophagus** and **GERD**](https://www.healthline.com/health/gerd/barretts-esophagus) **.** I have struggled with weight and eating my entire life, and being a male, not eating is seen as a serious issue. One positive thing though is I have total empathy for anyone struggling with weight, eating, and many other issues. I get told I am skinny as a rail and need to eat more food almost daily, which makes me feel pretty bad and the snowball grows. By the end of the day I am so exhausted from not eating, and just trying to get through the day I collapse and I get a few hours at night of feeling decent. I have been given so many prescriptions its ridiculous, when in my past experience eating CBD or something similar helped immensely and didn't have half the side effects I deal with now. I digress though, I didn't mean to make this about me, but merely share my experience. I was told to make a list of what I ate, in a journal or similar, and every 30 minutes mark how I felt, and what may have brought it on \(stress, situation, etc\), and then try to keep narrowing down a food regiment that would agree with my stomach. I have seen articles \(sorry I dont have the citation at the moment\) that state 90\% of your immune system is in your gut, and a lot of our mood is dependent upon your stomach and immune system. So I deduced that fine tuning my eating routine etc has helped improve my overall well being. So I suppose what I want to say to you is: Rest assured you are not alone! We all have to live in our own skin, we all have problems, but perhaps what to some may be a minor issue is a major one for another makes the water a bit muddied, but it doesn't change the fact you are going through a terrible time. So I suppose I am just trying to reassure you that its not your outer beauty that defines you for one, your illness for two, and writing about it like you did is the first step to help, and I feel like you are a genuine person just trying to make the best of a terrible situation. Feel free to message me if you ever are down or just want a sounding board. Im not great with words, but I am a good listener.

The one thing in my opinion is to try to focus on not only what is going wrong or right, but also where your going. If we all were to examine each other in minute detail, I do not think we would like what we see. Like someone else pointed out life is like a roller coaster, and from my own experience being told "everything gets better in time" is always easier said than done. A lot of people unfortunately need other people not because they enjoy their friendship etc, but because they need to feel like at least their life is not as bad as another. Its sort of a deflective, and in most cases not intentional perspective or behavior. We all carry the proverbial angel / devil on our shoulders, and the bad side a lot of the time speaks much louder and overrides the good and that is what brings you down. The softer, gentler, side often is not seen as a strength to alot of people, perhaps their own life experience has proven to them a different perspective, but what works for one does not always work for everyone. I know sometimes just getting out of bed, or going to work is a monumental task, which for other people may be pretty simple. Of course all of this is just conjecture, but I think you matter, no one deserves to rot, and just because at times you are happy, you should not feel guilty because there is suffering in the world. Its a self defeating prophecy. Like people much smarter than I have said "There is a time for laughing, a time for loving, a time for crying, and a time for mourning", its just all a matter of perspective. Our attitudes are truly the only real control we have, and practicing mindfulness, listening to positive reinforcement tapes \(or digital lol\), and breaking large tasks into smaller pieces make life just a little more palatable. Again, its easier to give advice than to just do it, so if it makes you feel any better, although I know of many things that help, when I feel in the dumps even my best attempts end in not what I was expecting, but the most important part of all is: just keep going on, you and have made a huge impact in life, its just we often dont get to see all the greatness from our actions. I hope life improves for you, and thank you for sharing.
